subject: Audit evidence pack deliverables + export format checklist
messages:
From: Janelle Ortiz <janelle@medicohealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: MedicoHealth Security <sec@medicohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: access ledger sample + schema (post-demo)

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Security team requested a concrete example of the "who/what/when" export you mentioned during the call so they can validate retention and PII handling against our compliance checklist. Two asks from our side: 

1) Sample export showing a short time window (one day) with the field-level schema and minimal real rows so we can verify the columns and formats (CSV and JSONL are both fine). Please include which internal IDs map to user identities and whether any fields are pseudonymized by default.

2) A short matrix that states retention defaults, supported retention windows (e.g. 30/90/365 days), and the ability to pull historical snapshots for legal holds. Also confirm: do audit logs include IP, session id, requester role, and model identifier?

Attached is a stub of the schema we expect for examples (we don't need actual customer data). Can you also confirm an estimated delivery timeline and the preferred delivery mechanism (S3 link, secure Drive share, or encrypted email)?

Thanks — we want to close this in the next cloud-security review.

Best,
Janelle Ortiz
Security Lead — MedicoHealth

Attachments: requested-sample-who-when-20270601.jsonl (please send sample), medico-security-checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Janelle Ortiz <janelle@medicohealth.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: access ledger sample + schema (post-demo)

Hi Janelle — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick summary / next steps from our side: 

- We can provide both CSV and JSONL sample exports. We'll include a header-level schema CSV explaining each column.
- Default audit fields we include: timestamp (ISO8601); actor_id (internal user id); actor_type (service/engineer/app); role (api_key/app/user); model_id; request_id; operation; object_id; ip_address; session_id; bytes_in/out. For PII fields, we will show how we pseudonymize user identifiers and which columns we omit/redact by default.
- Retention: out-of-the-box retention policies are 30/90/365 days; we support custom retention on Dedicated/Private plans and legal-hold snapshots for exports.

Plan: Aisha will prepare a small one-day sample (two dozen rows) in JSONL and CSV, plus a "schema map" CSV that defines each field and redaction behavior. We'll deliver via secure S3 pre-signed link. Target delivery: 3 business days (by Mon, 28 Jun). If you need it faster, let me know and we can prioritize.

I've looped in Aisha (compliance lead for exports) and Sean (solutions engineer) — tagging them for ETA and any format questions.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference

Attachments: redwood-audit-schema-v1.csv

> > Thanks for the demo earlier. Security team requested a concrete example ...

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
To: Janelle Ortiz <janelle@medicohealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: access ledger sample + schema (post-demo)

Hi Janelle —

Per Vanessa's note, attached is a small sample (three examples) exported from our test tenant that mimic the one-day window you requested. Notes below: 

- Export formats: CSV (columnar) and JSONL (line-delimited). We include a header file (redwood-audit-schema-v1.csv) that explains each column and indicates default redaction.
- Pseudonymization: actor_id in the sample is irreversibly hashed; we include an additional column (actor_identity_kinds) to show whether it maps to a user account, service key, or system process. We do not include raw email or un-hashed PII fields in the default export.
- Retention & holds: default buckets are 30/90/365; for legal hold we can generate a snapshot export (point-in-time) and keep it in encrypted S3 for the time the hold is active. Snapshot exports include full audit rows (subject to DPA) — we will coordinate any DPA requirements with your procurement/security teams.
- Fields included: timestamp, request_id, actor_id (hashed), actor_type, role, model_id, operation, object_id, ip_address, session_id, bytes_in, region. We can add additional telemetry on request (e.g., user agent).

Delivery: we'll stage the files to a pre-signed S3 location and share the link plus an HMAC. ETA: EOD Mon, 28 Jun. If you require a DocuSign DPA before receiving any PII-like samples, flag that now and we'll route to legal.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Compliance & Exports Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: requested-sample-who-when-20270601.jsonl, sample-who-when-20270601.csv, redwood-audit-schema-v1.csv

Vanessa / Aisha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications before you send the sample: 

- For HIPAA: we need a short statement that the sample contains no PHI and that any mapping tables that could re-identify users will not be shared without a signed DPA.
- Could you include a short example row that demonstrates an "elevated access" event (admin role performing export) and show which fields are present for that event? That helps our auditors verify role-based access logging.
- Delivery preference: pre-signed S3 is fine; please include a README in the export that lists the file checksums and schema version.

If all of that is doable, we'll mark this as satisfactory for the upcoming security review. I'll loop procurement if we need a DPA before sample delivery.

Thanks,
Janelle Ortiz
Security Lead — MedicoHealth
